title: The Model Decides, the Tool Does: Three Rules for an Agent That Designs Circuit Boards
excerpt: Our first hardware agent wrote files that looked right. We rebuilt Coppr around three rules enforced in code: only deterministic tools write artifacts, specialists return typed results instead of transcripts, and a run is complete only when verification says so.

title: Jevify: Teaching Open Models to Answer in Probabilities
excerpt: I built jev-bench - 166,054 real human-labeled rows - to check whether a decision model's probabilities can be trusted, and Jevify to turn open LLMs into ones that can. Plain fine-tuning made models contradict themselves; a coherence penalty cut that tenfold at no accuracy cost, and open models now beat Jev on accuracy, calibration and self-consistency.

title: TriZ: The Startup That Taught Me What to Build
excerpt: My first startup was a privacy-first smart home that worked in isolation from the internet. We built it, pitched it at UPenn, and got incubated - then hardware iteration speed became the wall. That bottleneck is why I'm building Coppr.

title: Cosmic Duck: Giving My AI OS a Body
excerpt: I bought a robot duck. My AI saw the email before I did and asked for a body. Here's what happens when a proactive AI OS gets eyes, a voice, and legs.

title: Why Coppr? The Case for Compiling Hardware
excerpt: The next great hardware tool will not hide engineering judgment. It will make intent executable, verification continuous, and every board easier to improve.

title: Building COSMIC: A Personal AI OS
excerpt: What happens when you try to build an AI that truly knows you?

title: THALAPATHY: From Silver Screen to Political Arena
excerpt: A name that once resonated in movie theaters is now echoing through the streets, homes, hearts and the whole State of Tamil Nadu.
